verdict.rationale: Secureframe's API reference has a documented Versioning section. Additive changes stay backwards compatible, and breaking changes require a new dated API version. That establishes versioned APIs and a compatibility policy, but the evidence never describes how old versions are deprecated or retired. missing for 10: documented deprecation/sunset timelines and notice periods for retiring API versions, guidance on how to pin or select a dated version, a changelog of releases, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: Backwards _incompatible_ changes require Secureframe to release a new dated API version, as the[y] can potentially break an integration.
Secureframe makes many additive API changes that are _backwards compatible_ and able to be supported in all API versions
Secureframe exposes a REST API for use by customers, partners, and community developers.
